title: Pixels To Prognosis
description: About the Event Gliomas are among the most aggressive brain tumours, and outlining them accurately on MRI is central to diagnosis, surgical planning and treatment monitoring. Doing it by hand is slow, and different radiologists often draw the boundaries differently. Pixels to Prognosis asks you to build an AI system that does this automatically. Using multimodal brain MRI scans, your model has to locate a glioma and separate it into its three subregions: active (enhancing) tumour, necrotic core, and surrounding edema. The event combines neuroscience, MRI physics and computer vision. You’ll need more than a model with a good leaderboard score. You’ll also need to understand what the scans show, why models fail, and how to make one that holds up on real clinical data. Who Can Participate Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students from any college and any stream Especially suited to students in Biotechnology & Biomedical Engineering, Computer Science, and AI & Data Science Teams of 1 to 3 members . Cross-disciplinary teams are encouraged. Competition Structure Round 1: Online Quiz (Screening) This is a case-based quiz on: How MRI machines work and the basics of MRI imaging The biology of brain gliomas and how they appear on MRI scans Artificial Intelligence, Deep Learning and Image Processing The questions reward reasoning over memorisation. The quiz is meant to sharpen your problem-solving for the later rounds. Round 2: Model Submission Round Shortlisted teams train a segmentation model on a curated glioma dataset we provide, [derived from the BraTS 2021 challenge]. Each patient has four MRI modalities: T1-weighted, post-contrast T1-weighted (T1ce), T2-weighted and T2-FLAIR. Your model must segment three regions: Whole Tumour, Tumour Core and Enhancing Tumour. Models are ranked on a hidden patient-level test set . Rules: Train only on the dataset provided. No external data. All learnable parameters must start from random initialisation . Pretrained weights are not allowed. You may use published architectures such as U-Net variants. The Colab notebook runtime must be 9 hours or less . Submission requirements: Complete source code (.py / .ipynb) Final trained weights (.pt / .keras) Training logs, including loss and validation curves, config and seed used (.csv) A technical report (.pdf) covering your thought process, pipeline, architecture details and the compute you used Evaluation: Segmentation quality is measured with the Dice score and 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance for each tumour region. Scoring also covers anatomical consistency, false-positive control, and the quality of your technical report. Finals: Offline Round at IIT Madras Finalists come to campus and receive a new set of MRI scans with real-world problems. These can include motion artefacts, missing modalities, or pathologies your model has never seen. Each team must: Work out what is wrong with the data and why it happened Adapt the model through preprocessing, retraining or other corrective strategies Present the problems they found, the medical reasoning behind them, and how they handled them Evaluation criteria: Problem identification and medical reasoning Model adaptation strategy and outcome Clarity of presentation and understanding Knowing when your model should not be trusted counts in your favour. Flagging an unreliable case for expert review is part of good clinical AI. Prizes & Recognition Cash prizes for the top 3 teams [prize pool: ₹35000] Special Awards for Best Robust Model and Best Diagnostic Reasoning Certificates of Merit for the winners(Hard Copy) Certificates of Merit for all finalists(Soft Copy) Certificates of Participation for all Round 2 participants Important Dates Registration closes: 28th December, 2026 Round 1 (Online Quiz): 5th December, 2026 Round 2 submission window: 9th - 16th December, 2026 Finals at IIT Madras: 4th January, 2027

title: WebClone Mania
description: Event Overview WebCloneMania is a web development competition designed to test participants' frontend development, debugging, and problem-solving skills. The event will feature two segments: Beginner and Advanced , allowing participants to compete based on their skill levels. Beginner Segment – Website Recreation: Participants will recreate a reference website revealed by the organisers at the beginning of the competition, focusing on visual accuracy, responsiveness, and functionality. Advanced Segment – Debug and Deploy: Participants will receive a pre-written codebase containing bugs, incomplete features, and backend issues. They must identify and fix the issues, implement the required functionality, and ensure the application works as intended. Eligibility and Participation Participation is individual; team formation is not permitted. Students from any college are eligible to participate. Participants from any academic year or specialization may participate. Participants must register for the appropriate segment according to the registration instructions provided by the organisers. Each participant may compete individually and must submit their own work. Segment 1: Beginner – Website Recreation Format Participants will be shown a reference website on the spot and must recreate it within the allotted time. Rules The reference website will be revealed immediately before the challenge begins. Participants will have approximately 3–4 hours to complete the challenge, subject to the final schedule announced by the organisers. Participants may use HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, Next.js, or other permitted frontend technologies. AI tools, coding assistants, libraries, frameworks, and official documentation are permitted. Participants must develop their own implementation during the competition. Submitting a pre-built clone or copying another participant's work is prohibited. Unauthorised external assistance is not permitted. The final website must be functional and accessible for evaluation. Submission Requirements Each participant must submit: Source Code: A GitHub repository containing the complete project. Live Website: A deployed website link or clear instructions to run the project locally. Demonstration Video: A short video demonstrating the completed website. Participant Details: Name, registration details, and other information requested by the organisers. All submissions must be completed before the announced deadline. Segment 2: Advanced – Debug and Deploy Format Participants will receive an existing codebase containing intentional bugs, broken functionality, incomplete implementations, or backend integration issues. Their task is to analyse the code, identify the problems, implement the required fixes, and make the application work correctly. Rules The starter codebase and problem statement will be provided by the organisers at the beginning of the challenge. Participants will have approximately 3–4 hours to debug, implement, test, and demonstrate their solutions. The codebase may include frontend, backend, database, API integration, authentication, or other web application components. Participants must identify and fix the issues in the provided code rather than replace the entire project with an unrelated implementation. Participants may use permitted programming languages, frameworks, debugging tools, AI coding assistants, and official documentation. Participants must understand and be able to explain their changes during evaluation. Unauthorised external assistance, copying another participant's solution, or sharing solutions during the competition is prohibited. The final application must run successfully and satisfy the requirements specified in the problem statement. Participants must submit their corrected codebase and demonstrate the working application before the deadline. Submission Requirements Each participant must submit: Source Code: A GitHub repository containing the corrected project. Working Application: A live deployment, where feasible, or a locally running application for evaluation. Demonstration: A short video or live demonstration showing the fixes and working features. Participant Details: Name, registration details, and other information requested by the organisers. Evaluation Criteria Beginner Segment Visual similarity to the reference website. Layout, typography, colours, and styling. Responsiveness across screen sizes. Functional interactions and navigation. Code quality and overall completeness. Advanced Segment Correct identification and resolution of bugs. Successful implementation of required features. Frontend–backend integration and API functionality. Application stability, error handling, and testing. Code quality, efficiency, and completeness. Ability to explain the implemented fixes. The organisers will announce the final scoring weights and evaluation procedure at the event. Fair Play and Disqualification Copying another participant's work or submitting someone else's implementation is prohibited. Unauthorised collaboration or external assistance is not allowed. Participants must not interfere with another participant's system, code, or submission. Misrepresenting work or exploiting the evaluation process may result in disqualification. The organisers reserve the right to disqualify participants who violate the rules. General Instructions Participants must bring their own laptops and ensure their development environments are ready. Participants should arrive at the venue before the scheduled start time. Internet access will be provided subject to availability. The organisers will communicate the exact timings, problem statements, submission links, and scoring weights before the competition begins. All decisions made by the organising team regarding the conduct and evaluation of the event will be final.

title: Shaastra Aerial Robotics Challenge
description: Competition Overview :  The Shaastra Aerial Robotics Challenge (SARC) is an exciting drone competition that brings together aspiring engineers, robotics enthusiasts, and innovators to test their drone-building skills, flying precision, and technical knowledge. Participants will navigate challenging obstacle courses, perform precise aerial manoeuvres, and compete in time-based challenges that test their control, stability, accuracy, and problem-solving abilities Competition Rounds: Round 0: Preliminary Submission: Teams must submit a flight demonstration video and a technical PDF for initial evaluation. The video must demonstrate: Smooth take-off and stable hovering. Stable flight while carrying a 50 g payload. Navigation through at least one hoop-shaped obstacle without contact. A precise 90° turn. Safe landing at the designated point. The technical PDF must include drone dimensions, total weight, power source specifications, manual control system details, safety mechanisms, and other relevant technical information. Selected teams will advance to Round 1. Round 1: Obstacle Course Challenge Qualified teams must navigate a specially designed obstacle course while maintaining stable, low-altitude flight. The course includes: Semicircular and quarter hoops. Diagonal split rectangular hoops. Sharp 90° turns. Double quarter hoops. Crossover and split semicircular hoops. Triangular and freely hanging circular hoops. T-rod obstacles. Teams must complete the obstacle sequence, cross the finish line, and land at the designated point. Scoring is based on course completion, time bonuses, and penalties for rule violations. Round 2: Checkpoints Challenge The top-performing teams from Round 1 will qualify for this timed challenge. Reach as many checkpoints as possible within the allotted time. Follow the obstacle-course rules applicable to Round 1. Earn 10 points for each successful checkpoint. Avoid unnecessary contacts and unsafe manoeuvres. The number of qualifying teams will be determined by the organisers based on participation. Round 3: Payload Delivery Challenge Teams will carry an organiser-provided payload through the obstacle course and release it onto a marked target area. Scoring would consider course completion, delivery accuracy, time bonuses, and penalties. Rules and Regulations: Drone type: Only multirotor drones, such as quadcopters and hexacopters, are permitted. Control system: Drones must be operated manually using a remote controller. Autonomous flight is not permitted.3. Dimensions: The drone must not exceed 1 metre and must not be smaller than 0.3 metre in any direction. Flight altitude: Drones must not exceed a height of 1.5 metres and must follow the prescribed arena boundaries and safety-net restrictions. Flight performance: Drones must demonstrate stable hovering, precise low-altitude flight, and controlled manoeuvrability. Obstacle contact: Contact with hoops, rods, will attract penalties. Ground contact: Touching the ground during the course will attract penalties. Arena boundaries: Exiting the arena boundaries may result in disqualification. Unsafe contacts: Exceeding the permitted number of unsafe contacts may result in disqualification. Drone crashes: A crash that prevents continuation may result in disqualification. FPV camera: An FPV camera is optional and is not mandatory. Arena Specifications: Arena dimensions: 8 m × 11 m × 1.25 m. Clearly marked start and finish points will be provided. Obstacle dimensions and placements will have a tolerance of ±5%. Eligibility: Students, robotics enthusiasts, and teams interested in drone technology, aerial robotics, and engineering innovation are encouraged to participate, subject to the final eligibility criteria announced by the organisers. Participants must ensure that their drones comply with the technical specifications and safety requirements. Scoring and Evaluation: Round 1 awards 100 base points for course completion, with time bonuses and penalties. Round 2 awards 10 points per successful checkpoint, subject to applicable penalties. Round 3 awards 80 base points for course completion, with time bonuses and penalties. The detailed scoring criteria and final competition format will be governed by the official rulebook. Only winners will receive hard-copy certificates, while participation and finalist certificates will be provided in soft-copy format.

title: AGENTX 2.0
description: AGENTX 2.0 is a national-level hackathon organized by HackQube, bringing together students, developers, AI enthusiasts, and innovators to build intelligent, technology-driven solutions to real-world challenges. The hackathon focuses on Artificial Intelligence, AI Agents, Agentic AI, Generative AI, and intelligent automation. Participants will have the opportunity to transform ideas into functional prototypes that demonstrate innovation, technical excellence, practical applicability, and real-world impact. Participants must select one of the official problem statements and develop a solution that addresses the specified challenge. Eligibility Criteria Students enrolled in recognized colleges or universities are eligible to participate. Developers, AI enthusiasts, and aspiring innovators may participate, subject to the registration requirements. Participants must provide accurate information during registration. All participants must comply with the hackathon rules and submission guidelines. Team Formation Rules Team Size: 2–4 members per team. Inter-college Teams: Allowed. Team members may belong to different colleges or universities. Inter-specialization Teams: Allowed. Members from different academic disciplines and technical specializations may collaborate. Each participant may be part of only one team. Teams must provide accurate details for all members during registration. One team must submit only one project for evaluation. Official Problem Statements Teams must select one of the following eight problem statements and develop a solution aligned with its objectives. PS01: Agentic Workflow Automation Build an AI agent that automates repetitive tasks by planning multi-step workflows, integrating external tools and APIs, executing actions, and verifying task completion. PS02: Autonomous AI Software Engineer Develop an AI agent that analyzes codebases, identifies bugs, proposes fixes, runs tests, and generates actionable reports to improve software development workflows. PS03: Multi-Agent Research & Fact-Checking Create a multi-agent system that researches complex topics, verifies information using reliable sources, identifies conflicting claims, and generates evidence-backed reports. PS04: Personalized AI Learning Agent Build an intelligent learning agent that identifies knowledge gaps, creates personalized learning paths, generates assessments, and adapts recommendations based on student progress. PS05: AI Operations Agent for Businesses Develop an AI agent that streamlines business operations by analyzing data, managing routine workflows, identifying exceptions, and recommending actions with appropriate human oversight. PS06: AI-Powered Cybersecurity Triage Create a defensive AI agent that analyzes security logs, correlates alerts, detects suspicious activities, and recommends safe remediation steps. PS07: Smart Energy & Sustainability Agent Build an AI agent that analyzes energy consumption data, identifies inefficiencies, predicts potential wastage, and recommends actionable sustainability improvements. PS08: Startup Co-Pilot Agent Develop a multi-agent system that assists early-stage founders with market research, competitor analysis, customer profiling, idea validation, and execution planning. Competition Format The competition will follow the official schedule and format announced by HackQube. The proposed process includes: Registration: Eligible participants register through Unstop in teams of 2–4 members. Problem Statement Selection: Each team selects one official problem statement from PS01 to PS08. Solution Development: Teams design and develop their solutions using appropriate technologies, APIs, frameworks, and AI tools. Project Submission: Teams submit the required project details and demonstration materials before the official deadline. Evaluation: Judges assess projects according to the published evaluation criteria. Final Results: Winners are determined based on evaluation scores and the final decision of the judging panel. The round-wise schedule, duration, submission deadline, and grand finale details will be communicated through official event announcements. Project Submission Guidelines Each team must submit the materials specified by the organizers. These may include: Project title and selected problem statement. Problem overview and proposed solution. Key features and explanation of the approach. Working prototype or functional demonstration. Source-code repository link, if required. Presentation or pitch deck, if required. Technology stack, APIs, frameworks, and AI tools used. Explanation of the solution's feasibility, impact, and scalability. All required submissions must be completed before the official deadline. Late or incomplete submissions may be disqualified. Judging Criteria Projects may be evaluated on the following parameters: Innovation: Originality and creativity of the proposed solution. Technical Implementation: Quality, functionality, and effective use of AI and other technologies. Problem Relevance: Effectiveness in addressing the selected problem statement. Feasibility and Scalability: Practical applicability and potential for further development. User Experience: Usability, accessibility, and clarity of the solution. Presentation and Demonstration: Quality of the project explanation, working demo, and responses to judges' questions. The final scoring weights and any additional evaluation requirements will be communicated by the organizers. Rules and Code of Conduct All submissions must address one of the official problem statements. Plagiarism, fraudulent registrations, misrepresentation of contributions, and presenting copied work as original are prohibited. Teams must disclose relevant third-party code, datasets, APIs, AI models, and tools used in their projects when requested. Participants must have the necessary rights and permissions to use submitted code, content, datasets, and other materials. Projects must comply with applicable laws, ethical technology practices, and data privacy requirements. Unauthorized system access, malicious activities, and misuse of data or services are strictly prohibited. Cybersecurity solutions must remain defensive and operate only within authorized environments. Teams must not submit multiple entries under different team identities unless explicitly permitted by the organizers. Participants must maintain professional conduct and respect fellow participants, mentors, judges, and organizers. The organizers reserve the right to investigate violations and disqualify teams that breach the rules. The judges' decisions will be final, subject to the published competition rules. Prizes and Recognition Prize details, certificates, special recognitions, and other benefits, if applicable, will be announced through official HackQube communications and the Unstop opportunity page. Only prizes and benefits explicitly confirmed by the organizers should be considered guaranteed. Important Information Opportunity: AGENTX 2.0 — National-Level Hackathon Organizer: HackQube Registration Platform: Unstop Team Size: 2–4 members Inter-college Participation: Allowed Inter-specialization Participation: Allowed Problem Statements: 8 Competition Format: As announced by the organizers Event Date: 14 November 2026 Venue: As announced by the organizers Registration Deadline: As announced by the organizers Participants are responsible for reviewing official announcements, completing registration correctly, and meeting all applicable deadlines. Any updates to the schedule, format, or rules will be communicated through the designated official channels. Build. Innovate. Elevate. Organized by HackQube — A Builders-First Technology Ecosystem.
